_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.355 (Default) with firmware rev27v-followup-339.

Firmware339 corrects the pulse-cadence detector that steers actuator pulse filtering and the refill pulse model. Without pulses, firmware338 reported a false 30-37 or 115-175 bpm cadence and never cleared a rate. Firmware339 analyses cadence only with the pump quiet for 8 seconds and the cuff above 20 mmHg, requires a confirming repeat at twice the period, holds a confirmed rate for at most 15 seconds while it cannot measure, and reports no cadence after three failed analyses. Constant-pressure settling bleeds and top-ups now also allow for the rate measured during the action itself, so a faster-than-expected bleed stops on time. Calibration, gains, feedforward and valve limits are unchanged.

Bench evidence on Device D (wrist cuff on syringe, ProSim): cadence read at refills 72/40/120 bpm with the simulator at 72/40/120 and 0 with pulses off; 14 of 14 constant-pressure landings started by the settling check within 8 seconds; deflation ratio and ramp RMS match firmware338. Large cuffs have not yet been measured with this firmware.

The update flashes the bundled firmware through the protected uploader, which snapshots and restores each controller's calibration and tuning.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
